what: Sanitized shape summary for the harness Monitor launch ack (claude-wire.md §E7) and ScheduleWakeup ack (§E8). Documentation summary, not a replayed wire log — shapes verified from the CLI's own session transcript of a live AO-managed stream-json session; the transcript's toolUseResult mirrors the wire's top-level tool_use_result (same relationship every E1-E6 shape uses). Go regression guards: TestAppendToolResultBlock_MonitorLaunchSetsBackgroundFlag, TestAppendToolResultBlock_TaskListAckNotBackground, TestAppendToolResultBlock_ScheduleWakeupEmitsSessionWakeup, TestAppendToolResultBlock_StringToolUseResultNoNewSignals (parse_user_test.go).

source.cli_context: Claude Code harness tools (Monitor / ScheduleWakeup / TaskCreate / TaskUpdate / TaskStop / TaskOutput) used by a headless stream-json session under AO

monitor_launch.ack_content_text: Monitor started (task bpzc8uiti, persistent — runs until TaskStop or session end). You will be notified on each event. Keep working — do not poll or sleep. ...
monitor_launch.notes: No run_in_background in input, no backgroundTaskId in the ack. taskId is the id the task lifecycle (task_started / task_notification / task_updated) routes by. Terminal via task_updated (TaskStop → status killed), same channel as E2.

task_list_ack_collision_guard.notes: TaskCreate/TaskUpdate acks carry a top-level taskId for a task-LIST row, not a process — bare taskId must never classify as a background launch. persistent/timeoutMs presence is the Monitor discriminator; surveyed against every toolUseResult key-shape in the capture session (17 distinct shapes).

schedule_wakeup.ack_content_text: Next wakeup scheduled for 14:31:00 (in 1559s). Nothing more to do this turn — the harness re-invokes you when the wakeup fires or a task-notification arrives.
schedule_wakeup.stop_ack_content_text: Loop stopped — no further wakeups scheduled. ...
schedule_wakeup.notes: scheduledFor is epoch MILLISECONDS. No task lifecycle exists behind the timer — the ack is the only wire signal that the session will resume itself. The fired wakeup arrives as a CLI-injected user turn (session-file queue-operation enqueue → queued_command attachment).
